messages.subject: Re: overlaying histograms legend?
parts:
Hi:

This is an example of 'creating a factor on the fly', illustrated in the ggplot2 book. 

ggplot(dat,aes(x=date)) + 
    geom_histogram(data=subset(dat,type == 'original'), aes(fill = "Original"), 
                             alpha = 0.5, binwidth =  1) +
    geom_histogram(data=subset(dat,type == 'subsample'), aes(fill = "Subsample"), 
                             alpha = 0.8, binwidth = 1) +
    labs(x = "Month", y = "Count", fill = "Data type") +
    ggtitle("Sampling Distributions\n")  +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "blue"))

The last line is to specify the colors you defined in your code.

Dennis

On Tue, Oct 30, 2012 at 9:49 AM, Nick <nick...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I'm new to ggplot and for the past couple of days I have been trying to figure out how to add a legend to a plot that has two histograms where one is overlaid on the other. Below is some fake data and the ggplot format that I have been using. Does anyone have any suggestions for how to add a legend to this plot?

dat1 <- data.frame(rnorm(n=8000, mean= 6, sd= 1))
colnames(dat1) <- "date"
dat1$type <- "original"
dat2 <- data.frame(rnorm(n=2000, mean= 6, sd= 1))
colnames(dat2) <- "date"
dat2$type <- "subsample"
dat <- rbind(dat1,dat2)

ggplot(dat,aes(x=date)) + 
  geom_histogram(data=subset(dat,type == 'original'),fill = "red", alpha = 0.5, binwidth =  1) +
  geom_histogram(data=subset(dat,type == 'subsample'),fill = "blue", alpha = 0.8, binwidth = 1) +
  ggtitle("Sampling Distributions\n") + xlab("Month") + ylab("Count")

Thanks,

Nick
